proof_summary: For \(p\equiv3\pmod4\), reindexing rows and columns by the nonzero quadratic residues rewrites the character matrix, up to a nonzero scalar, as \(U-U^{T}D\), where a multiplicative reindexing shows \(U\) is normal and \(D\) is a symmetric involution of determinant \(1\); an odd-dimensional determinant-symmetry argument then forces singularity. For \(p\equiv1\pmod4\), Euler’s criterion and the binomial theorem factor the matrix modulo \(p\) into invertible Vandermonde-type factors and a rank-one perturbation; Lagrange interpolation computes its remaining determinant factor, and Wilson’s theorem gives \(((p-1)/2)!^2=-1\), ruling out that factor’s vanishing.
